hypothesis: Each malformed exchange input (duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, overflow, wrong schema, oversize, truncated bytes, invalid UTF-8, wrong types, extra fields, forged identity) is refused by the relevant CIW validator.
mathematical_model: Validators: Workbench source.add (energy-accuracy), ciw.session.read_json, ciw.exchange.inspect_exchange (parsing stage, no SET checkout), ciw.exchange._identity, Session.from_workspace, Workbench.restore.
numerical_result: 19/21 malformed inputs refused with their declared CIW text (19 have one); the other 2 are counterexamples (incomplete-workspace.json: session_from_workspace: AttributeError; extra top-level workspace field (Session.from_workspace): accepted); read_json accepted 1e999 as inf and raised RecursionError on 20000-deep nesting; the extra top-level workspace field was dropped on re-save; committed fixtures match their generator.
observation_model: Refused (ValueError), crashed (any other exception) or accepted, exception type and exact message per validator (retained in malformed-refusals.json).

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

recommended_next_task: Deferred research question: apply the malformed matrix to the source parsers of the workbench kinds other than energy-accuracy, which parse after the same canonical-base64 and byte-budget checks; and, once CIW makes the changes docs/lab/EXCHANGE_BUNDLES.md requests (read_json refusing an overflowing number and turning RecursionError into ValueError, Session.from_workspace refusing unknown or missing top-level fields with a ValueError, source.add naming the source rather than a runtime), re-run it to check that each of the five counterexamples becomes a refusal with its own text.
